# Example verification policy (ADR-0007 Addendum 2 D23)

**This directory is example material, not real operator key material.** `example-signing-key.hex`
is a throwaway Ed25519 private key generated for this fixture only, committed deliberately so the
documented operator happy path (`docs/operations/screening-ledger-policy-signing.md`) is exercisable
end to end without `cmd/screening-ledger/main_test.go`'s in-test key generation being the only
example of a working policy in existence (CAP §7.8 named this absence explicitly: "no policy
artifact is committed"). A real deployment's signing key must never be committed -- generate one with
`screening-ledger-policy keygen` on an offline host and keep the private half out of this repository.

## Contents

- `example-signing-key.hex` -- the example Ed25519 private key (mode `0400`), hex-encoded.
- `example-public-key.hex` -- the corresponding public key, hex-encoded. This is what
  `--policy-public-key-file` points at when verifying `example-policy.signed.json`.
- `example-policy.signed.json` -- a `SignedVerificationPolicy` envelope for ledger ID
  `screening-api-v8g-example` (the same ledger ID as `test/fixtures/screening-ledger/state/`),
  produced by:

  ```sh
  screening-ledger-policy sign \
    --policy-file <an unsigned VerificationPolicy JSON document> \
    --private-key-file example-signing-key.hex \
    --output example-policy.signed.json
  ```

Regenerated by running the commands above; not hand-edited. If `VerificationPolicy`'s schema
changes (a `PACKAGE_SCHEMA_VERSION`-class event, per CLAUDE.md rule 6's spirit applied to this
document), this fixture is regenerated under the new schema in the same PR that changes it, not
left stale.
